restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 so that beta = beta* in every trial, Y4 ranges over the whole class of eta (524,288 values; no sub-class, no rule on h1), and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. Only outer steps that pass the exact filter of proof.md Section 8 for the six listed E1 outcomes S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0 are searched further (share 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782), and only those that the exact s-pattern pre-check keeps reach the joint solver; by Lemmas F and VP none of these steps loses a counted success. Successes with the eight other outcomes of beta* are not counted.

Heuristic part: a search over 2^90.117 walked trials (2^69.117 outer steps of 2^21, walked as 2^50.117 contexts of seven outer words with all 2^19 members of the class each, proof.md 9.8) for one whose remaining 128 chaining-value bits agree succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under H1', H4' and H5'.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, 64 registers, immediate constants; each fetch of a memory word costs one load. Outer steps are walked by contexts (proof.md 9.8): per context one fresh 256-bit word gives the seven outer words, the 39 lines of step CO that do not depend on the member run once (2,048 units charged per context), and all 2^19 members of the class are walked seven to a batch in packed 36-bit lanes, running in every batch only the eight lines that reach omega (Lemma Y2) and omega: 64 units per batch, counted and charged. The other 17 member lines (the Y9 closure) run on packed words in all seven lanes only at the first Q path of a batch, inside the Q path's charge. Both counts come from the submitted program's counting machine, whose self-test checks every lane against the scalar step CO and the filter and carries every lane bound (proof.md 9.3, 9.8).

The filter masks are read from two direct tables over all 2^32 words (Lemma DT; built once below 2^39 units, 2^38 bytes): at most 67 units per lane whose test-(2) mask meets S, charged 67 for every such lane up to E_BUDGET + 1 (the first Q path of a batch includes the 56-unit Y9 closure, a later one is at most 11), 512 per passing lane (rebuild, pre-check and credit test included), and for a step the pre-check keeps the proved cap C(T) <= 37,032 of the joint solver (proof.md 9.4) and root certificates, debited from a prepaid credit of 2,949,244,610,503,938,020,175 units before the solver runs: proved upper allowances of a specified layout, not measured counts, except the batch and Q path, which the program counts. No sorting; every read at a position given by a word (member lists, direct tables, VMASK, CT, transition arrays) is one charged load, and no table grows with the trials.

The run halts with failure when the test-(2) or pass count exceeds its budget, when C(T) exceeds the remaining credit, or after RUN_CONTEXTS contexts (RUN_BATCHES batches); budgets are charged at budget plus one and the solver at the whole credit, so the bound holds on every run (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

This package (v110) is entry b2d3e737 (winglock, v108, 64.92344) with two changes: the margin of H1' (i) is 11/10 in place of 7/5, as entry a402a477 (Jbenisek) declares on a preregistered reduced-width run (proof.md 13.10), so FACTOR = floor(10 * 138,512,695,296 / 11) = 125,920,632,087 and the run, both budgets and the credit shrink by 0.7857; the credit is the H5' mean bound ceil(1.06 * RUN_STEPS * cbar) plus a proved Bernstein reserve over contexts (tail exp(-20)) in place of 17/16 times it (proof.md 9.1, 10.3). The walk, its units, the success target, H1' (ii), H4' and H5' are unchanged. Entry b2d3e737 is entry e9b6649e (hecmas) with the Y9 closure moved into the Q path, folded context constants, interleaved member lists and the E count in a register; e9b6649e is entry 415e792c (Jbenisek) with the member loop and direct tables of proof.md 9.8.

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per context, whose first seven 32-bit words are the outer words; every context walks every member of the class exactly once (Lemma CX), so every mean over outer steps equals that of a uniform outer step (the sampler of entry 415e792c), while the outer steps of one context are dependent and only the contexts are independent; H1' (ii) is stated for contexts and the budgets and credit are reproved over contexts. Success 0.39 holds only under H1', H4' and H5'. The factor 125,920,632,087 in H1' is ten elevenths (v109; five sevenths in v108) of the model's conditional count of the six listed outcomes on the class, rounded down, and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments, which run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11): no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value.

The filter and the pre-check are exact; the shares of the two counts enter only the budgets (H4'), the mean of C(T) only the credit (H5'). No full 2-round collision is exhibited. The submitted program is this package's own (proof.md 9.2). Its root-instance experiments are those of the promoted entry dd91b2f6. Its self-test, which the organizer does not run, checks the counter construction, the filter for S with its exact counts, the walk of 9.8 (batch, Y9 closure and Q path) with its unit counts and lane bounds, and the ledger in exact integers. The pre-check, the credit, the joint solver layout and the certificate are defined in proof.md only, as in entries 415e792c and e9b6649e. The participant programs of proof.md Section 18 are entry e9b6649e's and are not run by the organizer.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, the beta* cube (beta*, mask, value), the seven tau values and eps of the filter's automata and the mask of S are what the search reads (73 bytes); the program also stores the two sub-class bits of its root instance (81 bytes of advice in all). The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by one exact count per model; beta* is the beta of that solution, and S has the least exact charge of the 16,383 nonempty outcome sets. preprocessing_log2 55 bounds the selection procedure of proof.md Section 12 (below 2^62.946 operations) in full and is included in time_log2: the search alone is below 2^64.5520 units. The selection, with this package's development charged in full (2^54 operations), is below 2^54.201. That the selection returns these values rests on records and a stated, unproved operation-rate bridge.

memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the code, the direct tables (2^38 bytes), selection, development (below 2^31 bytes) and search, all held at once (sum below 2^44).

Time: T = (64 RUN_BATCHES + 2,048 (RUN_CONTEXTS + 1) + 67 (E_BUDGET + 1) + 512 (PASS_BUDGET + 1) + CREDIT + once-only items + SEL + 2^54) / 430 + 2^38 = 2^64.55308119. That is below 2^64.55309 (2^6455308 < T^100000 < 2^6455309 in exact integers, checked by the self-test). Against entry e9b6649e's 128 per batch and 23 per Q path, the change is -0.44 bits.
No priority or novelty claim is made.
In the heuristics, 'the participant' and participant evidence mean the authors of entries 415e792c (Jbenisek) and, for proof.md 13.9, e9b6649e (hecmas); this package adds no measurement.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. Over the run's RUN_CONTEXTS independent contexts (one fresh uniform 256-bit word each; all 2^19 members of the class walked in every context, proof.md 9.8 and Lemma CX), let N_o be the number of listed good valid trials of one outer step (t != 0, R = 0, and an E1 outcome in S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0, six outcomes of beta*; Y4 in the whole class of eta; no rule on h1), counted over all of Q* whether or not the outer step passes the filter or the pre-check. (i) E[N_o] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = FACTOR * 2^-128, FACTOR = floor(10 * 138,512,695,296 / 11) = 125,920,632,087, about 2^-91.126 (just under ten elevenths of the conditional model rate p of Lemma S1 for S). (ii) The listed good trials of one context, within one outer step and across the outer steps (members) of the context, depend on each other weakly enough that the probability that no valid trial of the run is a listed good trial is at most exp(-0.49676) + 0.001. Given (i), with N_c the count of a context, rho_c = E[N_c(N_c-1)]/E[N_c] <= 0.0065 is sufficient for (ii) by Lemma S8 applied to the independent contexts; rho_c is the within-step ratio of entry 415e792c, averaged over the class, plus the cross-member part rho_x that the member loop adds (proof.md 10.3). By Lemma CX (c), part (i) is the same statement as in entry 415e792c: a context walks the whole class, so E[N_c] = 2^19 E[N_o] for a uniform outer step. This restates the rate-and-dependence premise of entry 26ebba63 for the whole class and S; that entry's accepted clause was for the sub-class of 2^17 members with rule A and seven outcomes and does not by itself imply this law: equal model counts and equal budget constants do not identify the law of N_o, and rho need not be the same (GPT Sol, answer AT 2). It is declared here anew. By Lemma F every listed good trial lies in an outer step that passes the filter, and by Lemma VP the pre-check skips no listed good trial, so N_o is the same count, pointwise (GPT Sol, answer AW 1); the rate per member of Q* of a passing outer step is q / pi_o, about 2^-81.148 if pi_o equals the exact share pi.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 a member of the whole class of eta (524,288 values, Lemma Q) walked over the whole class within each context of seven outer words drawn from the run's fresh 256-bit words (proof.md 9.8, Lemma CX), E1.c1 drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 in every trial, t solved per trial and t = 0 skipped. Only outer steps that pass the exact filter of Section 8 for S are searched further, and only those that the pre-check of 9.7 keeps reach the solver; N_o counts all of Q* in every outer step and only the six outcomes of S.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model of Section 10 with Y4 uniform in the class, of the part of beta* on the class carried by the six outcomes of S (67,633,152 = 1,032 * 2^16 on the per-trial scale 2^-83 of the class; the counting program and the six rows of its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1), taken at ten elevenths, rounded down (v109; the margin 11/10 of entry a402a477). The margin is supported by the preregistered reduced-width run of the counter arrangement made by the author of entry a402a477 and restated in proof.md 13.10: protocol fixed before the run (SHA-256 c5895dd64b07710f9fb386b0f9d4f6b5cb38b14b502a4cc80e51c60584432a4e), 40,960 runs and 3,235,715,578,385 counted trials at 8-bit words, 40,882 collisions of complete messages found against 40,800.63 predicted, ratio 1.00199 +- 0.00496, one-sided 97.7 per cent exact Poisson lower bound 0.99213 >= 10/11, SUPPORTED by the rule fixed in advance. The filter and the pre-check change neither the count nor the premise (Lemmas S9 (b) and VP). Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: a whole-class graphics-card run of 2^46 real counter trials in 2^25 passing outer steps, with a sub-class control of the same size, in which every measured quantity matches the exact model within 1.5 clustered standard errors, among them the E1 rate on the whole class of the seven outcomes of entry 59f8915e, 1.0020 +- 0.0086 of the model (13,595 events), and its ratio to the sub-class rate, 0.9895 +- 0.0120 (model 1); that counter covered the seven together, so the E1 event of S is a sub-event of the measured event (52/53 of it in the model) and was not counted on its own; 2^43 real trials inside passing outer steps of the seven-outcome filter on the sub-class, listed E1 outcome 0.979 +- 0.022 of its value; and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages, with no sub-class and no rule, in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted. The joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured at 32 bits. Member loop (proof.md 13.9, participant evidence, one run of SplitMix64, not preregistered): over 120,000 contexts, 6.29 * 10^10 outer steps with one trial each, the E1-side event that the E1 a-output difference is a tau of S, which every listed good trial meets, has per-context counts with the binomial variance (variance factor of the per-context rate v = 1.0000), as does the low-16-bit residual event R16 (v = 1.0007); the filter indicators are clustered by context with v = 1.143 and 1.152. Under the model E[N_c] is about 2^-51.1, so rho_x reaches 0.0065 only if v exceeds about 2^43.9 or a success at one member makes successes at other members of its context far more likely than the rate.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 125,920,632,087 is assumed (ten elevenths of the model count of the six outcomes of S on the class, rounded down). The margin 11/10 is a declared numerical clause, stronger than the margin 7/5 of entry b2d3e737, which does not imply it; its preregistered support (proof.md 13.10) is evidence at 8-bit words from another participant's run, not a transfer to 32 bits, and does not test the filter or the joint 128-bit event. If the count is exact the run has 0.5464 expected listed good trials, so the success bound tolerates rho_c only up to 0.187 (0.576 at 7/5). The accepted premise of entry 26ebba63 was for the sub-class with rule A; it is not inherited, and the whole-class law of N_o for S is declared, not proved. The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) of the same construction and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision, which no digest experiment can show. The transfer of the single-trial law to the actual sampler is partly proved (Lemmas S1-S5, S8, S9 and VP) and partly assumed in (i); the weak-dependence condition of (ii) is assumed, with a proved cap of 48 listed good trials in one outer step (Lemma CV). The whole-class graphics-card run measures the E1 side of the seven outcomes together and the filter, not the six of S on their own, not the E3 side (N3 four times that of the sub-class) nor the joint event, and its trials lie in passing outer steps of the fourteen-outcome filter, a superset of this filter's. Lemmas F and VP and Lemma S9 (a) use no law of the words; the 8-bit end-to-end run has no filter. The member loop adds the cross-member part rho_x of (ii), which is assumed: the measurement of proof.md 13.9 covers the filter, an E1-side event and a generic residual event, not the E3 side or the joint event, and it is one run of one generator made after the design.

heuristics.statement: Supporting. Two count-budget clauses with one failure allowance for their union: with probability at least 0.9995 over the coins both hold, so no budget halts the run. (a) Pass budget: at most PASS_BUDGET = 674,314,382,096,727,715 outer steps pass the filter for S (nominal share pi = 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782). (b) Lean test-(2) budget: at most E_BUDGET = 37,009,735,212,789,430,936 lanes have a test-(2) mask meeting S and run the Q path (nominal share 233,715,456 / 2^32 = 2^-4.1998). Each budget is ceil(17/16 * RUN_STEPS * share). Reaching a budget halts with failure; the time bound charges each budget plus one. The number of outer steps that reach the solver has no budget and no clause here: the solver is paid from the credit of H5prime-weighted-solver-work (GPT Sol, answer AW 5, which keeps these two count halts and replaces the third by the credit).
heuristics.scope: The counts N_E and N_2 of proof.md 10.3 over the RUN_STEPS outer steps of step 1 of Section 9.1, with Y4 drawn from the whole class: each is a sum over the independent contexts of per-context counts between 0 and 2^19 (Lemma CX), with mean 2^19 times the probability of its indicator for a uniform outer step; the two indicators of one outer step, and the indicators of the outer steps of one context, may depend on each other in any way.
heuristics.extrapolation: The nominal shares are exact for uniform independent (Y9, omega) (GPT Sol, answers AC, AN and AW 3; the certificate of Section 8). If each probability for a uniform outer step is at most 1.06 times its nominal share, the Bernstein inequality over the independent contexts, with a range of 2^19 per context, puts each overflow below exp(-B / (2 * 425^2 * 2^19 * (1 + 1/1275))) for its budget B: exp(-1.9 * 10^8) and exp(-3.5 * 10^6), so their union is below 2 * exp(-3.5 * 10^6), far below 0.0005. Measured (Section 13, untrusted by the harness, Python's generator, whole class): on 60,000,000 real outer steps the two counts are 1.0004 +- 0.0005 (test (2)) and 0.9980 +- 0.0041 (pass) of their nominal values; on another 30,000,000 the pass count is 0.9981 +- 0.0058 of its nominal value. With the seven-outcome filter on the sub-class the pass share was 1.00012 +- 0.00016 of its exact value on 2^35 outer steps. Under the member loop (proof.md 13.9, 120,000 contexts): 1.0011 +- 0.0011 (test (2)) and 1.0008 +- 0.0011 (pass) of their nominal values, with standard errors over contexts.
heuristics.limitations: That each sampler probability is at most 1.06 times its nominal share is not proved: the sampler's Y9 and omega are not proved independent and uniform. The measurements are runs of one generator made after the design, not a locked validation. The time bound, the filter and the pre-check do not depend on these shares.

heuristics.statement: Supporting (GPT Sol, answer AW 5: the premise H4-AS-v-S(eps), E_phys[V_S(U)] <= (1+eps) * cbar_S, at eps = 0.06). For an outer step U of the run, before any halt, let V(U) = C(T(U)), where T = X AND VMASK[nu] is the set of outcomes that the pre-check of proof.md 9.7 keeps and C is the proved cap of steps 2 and 3 for those outcomes (the restricted ledger 4,096 + 2,304 F + 1,152 A + 20 N_f + 48 N_r + 4 N_s + 368 Lf over the rows of T, Section 11; at most 37,032), with V(U) = 0 when T is empty or the step does not pass the filter. Premise: for a uniform outer step U (the sampler of entry 415e792c; in this package the mean over the outer steps of a uniform context, Lemma CX), E[V(U)] <= 1.06 * cbar, with cbar = 611,713,706,062,329 / 2^47 = 4.346487..., the exact mean of V in the counting model. It is one weighted moment over all outer steps, zeros included; it is not a mean of executed work, since V bounds the work of steps 2 and 3 in every outer step. Use (v110): before steps 2 and 3 the run debits C(T) from CREDIT = M_C + ceil(sqrt(40 L_C M_C)) + 14 L_C = 2,949,244,610,503,938,020,175, with M_C = ceil(1.06 * RUN_STEPS * cbar) and L_C = 2^19 * 37,032, and halts with failure when C(T) exceeds the remaining credit; under the premise, with independent contexts (Lemma CX) whose sums of V lie between 0 and L_C, so that the variance of the total is at most L_C M_C, the one-sided Bernstein inequality puts the probability that the credit is exhausted at or below exp(-20) (proof.md 10.3; v108 took 17/16 times the mean bound). The time bound charges the whole credit and does not depend on the premise; success 0.39 holds under H1', H4' and this premise (proof.md 10.4).
heuristics.scope: The values V(U) of the RUN_STEPS outer steps of step 1 of proof.md 9.1, walked by contexts (Lemma CX), each a function of its outer step, with Y4 drawn from the whole class of eta, S = 0x005f, the masks X of the filter of Section 8 and nu by formula (V) of 9.7; the mean is over all outer steps, passing or not.
heuristics.extrapolation: cbar is exact in the counting model M_v of proof.md 10.3: uniform independent (Y9, omega), as for the nominal shares of H4', and an independent uniform three-bit nu; cbar = sum over the masks A and nu of n_A C(A AND S AND VMASK[nu]) / 2^51 (GPT Sol, answer AW 5; rebuilt in integers by the participant from the program's own automata). Measured (proof.md Section 13, untrusted by the harness): a preregistered sample whose protocol, PREREG.txt with SHA-256 c862bfb1082e5236b0d9d81d6daef38e5f1135b27b25ad5c0093a1bf76455872, was written before the main run, of 2^28 = 268,435,456 real outer steps of the whole class (Python's MT19937, 32 seeds derived by SHA-256, one run, no interim look): mean of V 4.322858 against 4.346487, ratio 0.99456 +- 0.00405; one-sided upper bounds on the ratio 1.01059 (empirical Bernstein, delta 0.00135, range 37,032) and 1.01513 (bounded KL), both below 1.06, so the rule fixed in advance gives SUPPORTED at eps = 0.06. The largest V seen was 37,032, nu agreed with a separate computation in every step, and 0.24872 of the passing steps survived the pre-check against 1/4.
heuristics.limitations: Not proved: the sampler's nu is a function of the outer step and is not proved uniform or independent of the masks, so the model value cbar is not a property of the sampler. The sample is statistical evidence from one pseudorandom generator, run by the participant and not by the organizer's harness, on the counter instance that no organizer experiment runs; it supports eps = 0.06 and not eps = 0.0095. It does not test H1' or the two count clauses of H4'. If the premise fails, the credit can halt the run with failure, which lowers the success probability and not the time bound. This premise takes the place of the third count budget of entry 0bc5f130 of the same participant.
